name: Hotel Splendide Royal Rome
positioning: Baroque-styled hotel in a restored 19th-century building between Via Veneto and the gardens of Villa Borghese in Rome
best_for: Travelers who want an opulent, period-style base near Via Veneto and Villa Borghese
Guests who want a room with a terrace facing the Borghese Gardens

facts.text: The hotel is set between Via Veneto and the gardens of Villa Borghese.
The hotel is steps from Via Veneto and major works of art by Bernini and Borromini.
The shops and designer boutiques of Piazza di Spagna and Via dei Condotti are a few steps away.
The hotel occupies a restored 19th-century building.
The interiors display antique golden boiseries, rich brocade, polished marble and ornate stucco work.
The baroque-inspired bedrooms and suites have damask drapes, crimson carpets, period furniture, and antique mirrors and artworks in gilded frames.
Almost all rooms have large marble bathrooms with natural light.
Some suites have a private terrace overlooking Villa Borghese.
Mirabelle serves Mediterranean cuisine and offers dining on an outside terrace overlooking the gardens.
Three function rooms seat 10 to 50 participants, and a board room is located in the presidential suite.
The hotel is a member of the Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

highlights.text: About one third of the rooms have large walk-out terraces, most facing the Borghese Gardens.
The hotel sits in the Via Veneto area, on a hill directly above the historic centre of Rome, with views over the gardens of Villa Borghese.
The main lobby has floors of Italian marble, a huge Murano glass chandelier and baroque wall decoration.
The gourmet Mirabelle restaurant is on the 7th floor, with a view that takes in almost every monument of ancient Rome.
Rooms and suites feature Carrara marble bathrooms, antique furnishings and double-pane glass windows.

considerations.text: Only about one third of the rooms have walk-out terraces, so a terrace is not standard.
The decor is baroque-inspired, with damask drapes, crimson carpets and period furniture, not a contemporary minimalist look.
WhataHotel notes the historic building layout may mean room sizes vary.
